Chapter 11: Self-Care, Resilience, and the Importance of Community.
Let’s be honest—the work of confronting racism? It’s absolutely exhausting. For folks who are most affected, the toll goes so much deeper than just feeling tired. It’s physical, it’s emotional, and sometimes, it hits you right in the spirit. Maybe you know what it’s like to feel overwhelmed, or even lose hope, or just flat out burn out.
That’s why self-care isn’t some trendy buzzword. It’s a real necessity.
Imagine scrolling through the news, your heart racing with every headline. You want to do something—anything—but that helpless feeling? It creeps in fast. Most people never realize just how much energy it takes to keep moving forward when you’re faced with injustice, day after day.
The truth is, self-care looks different for all of us. Maybe it’s spending time with family or close friends. Maybe you find peace in art, or music, or those rare quiet moments alone. The important thing is: you find what helps you recharge, heal, and remember—you’re not in this by yourself.
That’s where community comes in. Community is where we find our strength. It’s where you’re understood, supported, and you get that sense of belonging. Think back to a time when you joined a local group, maybe feeling a bit unsure. The first meeting? Super awkward. But, over time, that group becomes your lifeline—a place to share your story, to celebrate the wins, and to mourn the losses together.
Resilience isn’t about pretending you never feel pain. It’s about figuring out how to keep going, even when things feel impossible. It’s about leaning on others, asking for help when you need it, and refusing to give up. Remember, the work of anti-racism—it’s a marathon, not a sprint. No one can do it alone.
